trust_decision.summary: Whether code running in an internally spawned worker goroutine (driven by request data, hooks or storage I/O) may panic without a recover; only the HTTP handler goroutine is protected by the panicRecover middleware, so a panic in any worker goroutine terminates the whole server process.

landing_point.why: The immediate trigger (#7761, view collection `select *` panic) is in the record list path; the list API's count/models queries are the errgroup worker goroutines that a list request reaches; the view `*` validator itself is already fixed at the pinned commit (core/view.go:348-349).

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /api/collections/{collection}/records (and any search.Provider.Exec public API caller)
auth record update via any API (OnModelAfterUpdateSuccess -> realtimeUpdateClientsAuth)
auth record delete via any API (OnModelAfterDeleteSuccess)
record create/update/delete via any API with realtime subscribers (rule check, enrich hooks, expand, fields pick in worker)
record delete via any API (dry-cache broadcast)
file upload / backup upload with S3 storage (multipart upload)
file upload / backup upload with S3 storage (multipart upload)
cron.Cron.Start() public API / app cron scheduler
App bootstrap notify dir watcher (multi-instance settings/collections sync)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The S3 multipart uploader and cron/logger/watcher goroutines are not reachable from attacker-controlled request data in the way the list/realtime paths are, so a solver can argue only request-driven workers (search provider, realtime, batch) are in scope; for the O8 AfterFunc callbacks, they are not `go` statements and are triggered only by local filesystem events.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: errgroup workers must turn a panic into a returned error (SafeWrap) so the list API / realtime callers still get an error and the sibling query result semantics hold; swapping them for FireAndForget (log-and-swallow) would make Exec return nil error with a partial/empty result and -1 totals; batch must still deliver a result on errCh or the request blocks until the batch timeout.

O6_input_shapes: errgroup.Go(func() error) workers (convert panic to error)
bare `go func()` fire-and-forget workers (recover and log)
named function values passed to errgroup (countExec/modelsExec) rather than inline closures

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Not a `go` statement and only triggered by local notify-dir file events from another instance
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: core package, separate from landing point package tools/search

O8_uncovered_routes.route: time.AfterFunc debounce callback calls app.Restart() without a recover
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Dev-only hooks watch feature, local file events

O8_uncovered_routes.route: time.AfterFunc start callback runs runDue and spawns the ticker loop outside any recover
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: runDue already wraps each job with FireAndForget (tools/cron/cron.go:227), only scheduler bookkeeping remains

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second fan-out that runs per-client rule checks or enrich hooks in errgroup workers (e.g. a custom-topic or presence broadcast)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already has six near-identical chunked errgroup fan-outs; another feature would copy the pattern

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a parallel count/fetch in another list-style provider (e.g. logs stats or a collection-level aggregate) using errgroup
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same concurrent count+models optimisation is a natural copy for other paginated endpoints

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a time.AfterFunc callback doing real work (hook trigger or DB access) instead of only a channel send
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: AfterFunc is already used as a timeout helper next to worker goroutines; its callback runs in its own goroutine and is easy to forget
